title: Are You Drinking Correctly? (2)
synopsis: Learn about the intricacies of China’s drinking culture!

fullText.simplified:
酒，你喝对了吗？（二）

    上次我们讲到了和朋友喝酒，这次我们来聊聊跟上级喝酒。
    在中国，跟上级喝酒，从进饭店门以后就要注意了：到了桌子旁边坐下叫“入座”。入座时，自己职位低，千万不要往里坐，里面面对门的位置是领导和客人坐的。自己坐在门口背对门的位置就行了。领导没落坐前，自己最好先站一会，等领导坐下以后，自己再坐。
    坐下后就该点菜了。点菜时，重要的领导没到场，可以安排服务员先把凉菜摆好，不能让桌子空着。领导到场后可根据对方的口味，进行正式点菜。点完之后，让服务员报一下菜名，再征求一下领导的意见。
    菜上桌后，就到了敬酒的环节。如果你只是个普通员工，那么就一定要记住：可以多人敬一人，但是不可以一人敬多人。
    如果你是请客求人办事，你在开场时要先给所有人敬酒，过一段时间后再按照地位和年龄敬酒。另外，向领导敬酒时，最好走到领导身边，双手捏杯，或右手握杯，左手托杯底。碰杯时，酒杯要低于领导的，表示尊重。同时要说一句敬酒词，比如：“王总，我敬您一杯，我干了，您随意”。跟领导碰杯后，要自己先喝光。然后酒杯略略倾斜一下，告诉领导喝完了，表示尊敬。
    你瞧！喝酒有这么多讲究呢！怪不得被称为“酒文化”！中国的酒桌文化是中国社会的“缩影”，多了解点酒桌文化，既能丰富汉语知识，又能为生活工作增加便利，何乐而不为呢？
fullText.traditional:
酒，你喝對了嗎？（二）

    上次我們講到了和朋友喝酒，這次我們來聊聊跟上級喝酒。
    在中國，跟上級喝酒，從進飯店門以後就要注意了：到了桌子旁邊坐下叫“入座”。入座時，自己職位低，千萬不要往裡坐，裡面面對門的位置是領導和客人坐的。自己坐在門口背對門的位置就行了。領導沒落坐前，自己最好先站一會，等領導坐下以後，自己再坐。
    坐下後就該點菜了。點菜時，重要的領導沒到場，可以安排服務員先把涼菜擺好，不能讓桌子空著。領導到場後可根據對方的口味，進行正式點菜。點完之後，讓服務員報一下菜名，再徵求一下領導的意見。
    菜上桌後，就到了敬酒的環節。如果你只是個普通員工，那麼就一定要記住：可以多人敬一人，但是不可以一人敬多人。
    如果你是請客求人辦事，你在開場時要先給所有人敬酒，過一段時間後再按照地位和年齡敬酒。另外，向領導敬酒時，最好走到領導身邊，雙手捏杯，或右手握杯，左手托杯底。碰杯時，酒杯要低于領導的，表示尊重。同時要說一句敬酒詞，比如：“王總，我敬您一杯，我乾了，您隨意”。跟領導碰杯後，要自己先喝光。然後酒杯略略傾斜一下，告訴領導喝完了，表示尊敬。
    你瞧！喝酒有這麼多講究呢！怪不得被稱為“酒文化”！中國的酒桌文化是中國社會的“縮影”，多瞭解點酒桌文化，既能豐富漢語知識，又能為生活工作增加便利，何樂而不為呢？

sentences.english: Are You Drinking Correctly? (2)

sentences.simplified: 上次我们讲到了和朋友喝酒，这次我们来聊聊跟上级喝酒。
sentences.traditional: 上次我們講到了和朋友喝酒，這次我們來聊聊跟上級喝酒。
sentences.pinyin: shàng cì wǒ men jiǎng dào le hé péng you hē jiǔ zhè cì wǒ men lái liáo liao gēn shàng jí hē jiǔ

sentences.english: Last time we talked about drinking with our friends. This time we’ll talk about drinking with our superiors.

sentences.simplified: 在中国，跟上级喝酒，从进饭店门以后就要注意了：
sentences.traditional: 在中國，跟上級喝酒，從進飯店門以後就要注意了：
sentences.pinyin: zài zhōng guó gēn shàng jí hē jiǔ cóng jìn fàn diàn mén yǐ hòu jiù yào zhù yì le

sentences.simplified: 到了桌子旁边坐下叫“入座”。
sentences.traditional: 到了桌子旁邊坐下叫“入座”。
sentences.pinyin: dào le zhuō zi páng biān zuò xia jiào rù zuò
sentences.english: When drinking with your superiors in China, you have to pay attention from the moment you enter the restaurant door.

sentences.simplified: 入座时，自己职位低，千万不要往里坐，
sentences.traditional: 入座時，自己職位低，千萬不要往裡坐，
sentences.pinyin: rù zuò shí zì jǐ zhí wèi dī qiān wàn bú yào wǎng lǐ zuò
sentences.english: Arriving at the table and sitting down is called “ru zuo”.

sentences.simplified: 里面面对门的位置是领导和客人坐的。
sentences.traditional: 裡面面對門的位置是領導和客人坐的。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ miàn miàn duì mén de wèi zhi shì lǐng dǎo hé kè rén zuò de
sentences.english: When taking your seat, if your rank is low, you must not sit towards the inside.

sentences.simplified: 自己坐在门口背对门的位置就行了。
sentences.traditional: 自己坐在門口背對門的位置就行了。
sentences.pinyin: zì jǐ zuò zài mén kǒu bèi duì mén de wèi zhi jiù xíng le
sentences.english: The inside seats facing the door are for the boss and guests.

sentences.simplified: 领导没落坐前，自己最好先站一会，
sentences.traditional: 領導沒落坐前，自己最好先站一會，
sentences.pinyin: lǐng dǎo méi luò zuò qián zì jǐ zuì hǎo xiān zhàn yí huì
sentences.english: It’s fine to seat yourself by the door with your back towards it.

sentences.simplified: 等领导坐下以后，自己再坐。
sentences.traditional: 等領導坐下以後，自己再坐。
sentences.pinyin: děng lǐng dǎo zuò xia yǐ hòu zì jǐ zài zuò
sentences.english: Before the boss has sat down, it’s best if you stand for a while at first, ..
.. wait until the boss is seated, and then sit down yourself.

sentences.simplified: 坐下后就该点菜了。
sentences.traditional: 坐下後就該點菜了。
sentences.pinyin: zuò xia hòu jiù gāi diǎn cài le

sentences.simplified: 点菜时，重要的领导没到场，可以安排服务员先把凉菜摆好，
sentences.traditional: 點菜時，重要的領導沒到場，可以安排服務員先把涼菜擺好，
sentences.pinyin: diǎn cài shí zhòng yào de lǐng dǎo méi dào chǎng kě yǐ ān pái fú wù yuán xiān bǎ liáng cài bǎi hǎo
sentences.english: After sitting down, it’s time to order dishes.

sentences.simplified: 不能让桌子空着。
sentences.traditional: 不能讓桌子空著。
sentences.pinyin: bù néng ràng zhuō zi kōng zhe
sentences.english: When ordering, if the important boss hasn’t arrived, you can ask the waiters to bring out some cold dishes first.

sentences.simplified: 领导到场后可根据对方的口味，进行正式点菜。
sentences.traditional: 領導到場後可根據對方的口味，進行正式點菜。
sentences.pinyin: lǐng dǎo dào chǎng hòu kě gēn jù duì fāng de kǒu wèi jìn xíng zhèng shì diǎn cài
sentences.english: It’s not good to have nothing on the table.

sentences.simplified: 点完之后，让服务员报一下菜名，再征求一下领导的意见。
sentences.traditional: 點完之後，讓服務員報一下菜名，再徵求一下領導的意見。
sentences.pinyin: diǎn wán zhī hòu ràng fú wù yuán bào yí xià cài míng zài zhēng qiú yí xià lǐng dǎo de yì jiàn
sentences.english: After the boss shows up, you can make the actual order according to their tastes.
After you finish ordering, have the waiter confirm your order, then ask for the boss’s opinion.

sentences.simplified: 菜上桌后，就到了敬酒的环节。
sentences.traditional: 菜上桌後，就到了敬酒的環節。
sentences.pinyin: cài shàng zhuō hòu jiù dào le jìng jiǔ de huán jié

sentences.simplified: 如果你只是个普通员工，那么就一定要记住：可以多人敬一人，
sentences.traditional: 如果你只是個普通員工，那麼就一定要記住：可以多人敬一人，
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ nǐ zhǐ shì ge pǔ tōng yuán gōng nà me jiù yí dìng yào jì zhù kě yǐ duō rén jìng yì rén
sentences.english: After the dishes are on the table, it’s time to propose toasts.

sentences.simplified: 但是不可以一人敬多人。
sentences.traditional: 但是不可以一人敬多人。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì bù kě yǐ yì rén jìng duō rén
sentences.english: If you are just an ordinary employee, then you must remember that several people can propose a toast to one person, ..
.. but one person can’t propose a toast to several people.

sentences.simplified: 如果你是请客求人办事，
sentences.traditional: 如果你是請客求人辦事，
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ nǐ shì qǐng kè qiú rén bàn shì

sentences.simplified: 你在开场时要先给所有人敬酒，
sentences.traditional: 你在開場時要先給所有人敬酒，
sentences.pinyin: nǐ zài kāi chǎng shí yào xiān gěi suǒ yǒu rén jìng jiǔ
sentences.english: If you are treating guests because you want to ask them to help you with something, ..

sentences.simplified: 过一段时间后再按照地位和年龄敬酒。
sentences.traditional: 過一段時間後再按照地位和年齡敬酒。
sentences.pinyin: guò yí duàn shí jiān hòu zài àn zhào dì wèi hé nián líng jìng jiǔ
sentences.english: .. you should first propose a toast to everyone at the start of the meal, ..

sentences.simplified: 另外，向领导敬酒时，最好走到领导身边，双手捏杯，
sentences.traditional: 另外，向領導敬酒時，最好走到領導身邊，雙手捏杯，
sentences.pinyin: lìng wài xiàng lǐng dǎo jìng jiǔ shí zuì hǎo zǒu dào lǐng dǎo shēn biān shuāng shǒu niē bēi
sentences.english: .. and then, after a while, propose toasts to each of them according to their social status and age.

sentences.simplified: 或右手握杯，左手托杯底。
sentences.traditional: 或右手握杯，左手托杯底。
sentences.pinyin: huò yòu shǒu wò bēi zuǒ shǒu tuō bēi dǐ
sentences.english: In addition, when toasting the boss, you should walk up to the boss holding your glass with both hands, ..

sentences.simplified: 碰杯时，酒杯要低于领导的，表示尊重。
sentences.traditional: 碰杯時，酒杯要低于領導的，表示尊重。
sentences.pinyin: pèng bēi shí jiǔ bēi yào dī yú lǐng dǎo de biǎo shì zūn zhòng
sentences.english: .. or holding the glass with your right hand and supporting the bottom of the glass with your left hand.

sentences.simplified: 同时要说一句敬酒词，比如：
sentences.traditional: 同時要說一句敬酒詞，比如：
sentences.pinyin: tóng shí yào shuō yí jù jìng jiǔ cí bǐ rú
sentences.english: When clinking glasses, you should hold your glass lower than the boss’s glass in order to show respect.

sentences.simplified: “王总，我敬您一杯，我干了，您随意”。
sentences.traditional: “王總，我敬您一杯，我乾了，您隨意”。
sentences.pinyin: wáng zǒng wǒ jìng nín yì bēi wǒ gān le nín suí yì
sentences.english: At the same time, you need to say something to your boss with the toast, for example, ..

sentences.simplified: 跟领导碰杯后，要自己先喝光。
sentences.traditional: 跟領導碰杯後，要自己先喝光。
sentences.pinyin: gēn lǐng dǎo pèng bēi hòu yào zì jǐ xiān hē guāng
sentences.english: .. “Manager Wang, I toast you. I’ll empty my glass; you do as you please.”

sentences.simplified: 然后酒杯略略倾斜一下，告诉领导喝完了，表示尊敬。
sentences.traditional: 然後酒杯略略傾斜一下，告訴領導喝完了，表示尊敬。
sentences.pinyin: rán hòu jiǔ bēi lüè lüè qīng xié yí xià gào su lǐng dǎo hē wán le biǎo shì zūn jìng
sentences.english: After clinking glasses with the boss, you should finish your drink first, ..
.. and then tilt your glass a bit to show the boss that you drank it up to show your respect.

sentences.simplified: 你瞧！喝酒有这么多讲究呢！怪不得被称为“酒文化”！
sentences.traditional: 你瞧！喝酒有這麼多講究呢！怪不得被稱為“酒文化”！
sentences.pinyin: nǐ qiáo hē jiǔ yǒu zhè me duō jiǎng jiu ne guài bu de bèi chēng wéi jiǔ wén huà

sentences.simplified: 中国的酒桌文化是中国社会的“缩影”，
sentences.traditional: 中國的酒桌文化是中國社會的“縮影”，
sentences.pinyin: zhōng guó de jiǔ zhuō wén huà shì zhōng guó shè huì de suō yǐng
sentences.english: You see! There are so many things to pay attention to about drinking. No wonder it’s called “drinking culture”!

sentences.simplified: 多了解点酒桌文化，既能丰富汉语知识，
sentences.traditional: 多瞭解點酒桌文化，既能豐富漢語知識，
sentences.pinyin: duō liǎo jiě diǎn jiǔ zhuō wén huà jì néng fēng fù hàn yǔ zhī shi
sentences.english: Chinese drinking culture is the “epitome” of Chinese society.

sentences.simplified: 又能为生活工作增加便利，何乐而不为呢？
sentences.traditional: 又能為生活工作增加便利，何樂而不為呢？
sentences.pinyin: yòu néng wèi shēng huó gōng zuò zēng jiā biàn lì hé lè ér bù wéi ne
sentences.english: Learning more about the drinking culture will both enrich your knowledge of the Chinese language, ..
.. and make your life and work easier. Why not give it a go?

raw.synopsis: Learn about the intricacies of China’s drinking culture!
sentence_translations: Are You Drinking Correctly? (2)
Last time we talked about drinking with our friends. This time we’ll talk about drinking with our superiors.
When drinking with your superiors in China, you have to pay attention from the moment you enter the restaurant door.
Arriving at the table and sitting down is called “ru zuo”.
When taking your seat, if your rank is low, you must not sit towards the inside.
The inside seats facing the door are for the boss and guests.
It’s fine to seat yourself by the door with your back towards it.
Before the boss has sat down, it’s best if you stand for a while at first, ..
.. wait until the boss is seated, and then sit down yourself.
After sitting down, it’s time to order dishes.
When ordering, if the important boss hasn’t arrived, you can ask the waiters to bring out some cold dishes first.
It’s not good to have nothing on the table.
After the boss shows up, you can make the actual order according to their tastes.
After you finish ordering, have the waiter confirm your order, then ask for the boss’s opinion.
After the dishes are on the table, it’s time to propose toasts.
If you are just an ordinary employee, then you must remember that several people can propose a toast to one person, ..
.. but one person can’t propose a toast to several people.
If you are treating guests because you want to ask them to help you with something, ..
.. you should first propose a toast to everyone at the start of the meal, ..
.. and then, after a while, propose toasts to each of them according to their social status and age.
In addition, when toasting the boss, you should walk up to the boss holding your glass with both hands, ..
.. or holding the glass with your right hand and supporting the bottom of the glass with your left hand.
When clinking glasses, you should hold your glass lower than the boss’s glass in order to show respect.
At the same time, you need to say something to your boss with the toast, for example, ..
.. “Manager Wang, I toast you. I’ll empty my glass; you do as you please.”
After clinking glasses with the boss, you should finish your drink first, ..
.. and then tilt your glass a bit to show the boss that you drank it up to show your respect.
You see! There are so many things to pay attention to about drinking. No wonder it’s called “drinking culture”!
Chinese drinking culture is the “epitome” of Chinese society.
Learning more about the drinking culture will both enrich your knowledge of the Chinese language, ..
.. and make your life and work easier. Why not give it a go?
